title: PARIS2, optimized photochemistry method to study dynamic in vivo RNA structuromes and interactomes
protocol: Wash cells in a 10 cm dish twice with 1X PBS.
Add 200 μL of 2X PBS and 200 μL of 1 mg/mL AMT to each dish.
Incubate cells at 37°C for 15 minutes.
Place ice trays in the cross-linker and put cell dishes on ice.
Irradiate cells with 365 nm UV light for 30 minutes, swirling plates every 10 minutes.
Remove cross-linking solution after irradiation and wash cells twice with 1X PBS.
Add 100 μL of 6 M GuSCN to each dish containing cells.
Lysate cells by vigorous manual shaking for 1 minute.
Add 12 μL of 500 mM EDTA, 60 μL of 10x PBS, and bring the volume to 600 μL with water.
Pass the sample through a 25G or 26G needle about 20 times.
Add proteinase K to 1 mg/ml.
Mix well and incubate at 37°C for 1 hour on a shaker at 600-900 RPM.
Manually shake the tubes during incubation to facilitate mixing.
After PK digestion, add 60 μL of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.3).
Add 600 μL of water-saturated phenol (pH 6.7) and mix well.
Divide into two tubes and add 600 μL of pure isopropanol to each tube.
Spin down the precipitate at 15000 rpm for 20 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and dispose of phenol waste properly.
Wash the precipitate with 70% ethanol twice.
Mix well and shake vigorously before spinning down in each wash.
Combine TNA pellets from two tubes.
Resuspend in 300 μL of nuclease-free water for each 10 cm plate of cells.
Determine the concentration and quality of the TNA sample using Nanodrop and Tape station.
Transfer 100 μg of TNA samples to a new tube.
Add 20 μL of 10X TURBO™ DNase Buffer.
Add 25 μL of TURBO™ DNase (2 Units/μL).
Bring each sample to a final reaction volume of 200 μL using H<sub>2</sub>O.
Incubate samples at 37°C for 20 min.
Add 20 μL of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.3), 220 μL of water-saturated phenol (pH 6.7), and 450 μL of pure isopropanol to each sample, mix well.
Spin samples for 20 minutes at 12,000 x g at 4°C.
Wash pellet twice with 70% Ethanol.
Resuspend RNA samples in 50 μL of RNase-free water.
Transfer 10 μg of DNase treated RNA sample to a new tube.
Add ShortCut mix (4 μL of 10x ShortCut buffer, 4 μL of 50 mM MnCl<sub>2</sub>, and 10 μL of ShortCut RNase III) to each sample, add RNase-free water up to 40 μL.
Incubate samples at 37°C for 5 mins.
Add 4 μL of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.3), 3 μL of GlycoBlue, and 60 μL of phenol to each sample, add 360 μL of pure ethanol, mix well.
Spin samples for 20 minutes at 12,000 x g at 4°C.
Wash pellet twice with 70% Ethanol.
Resuspend RNA in 10 μL of RNase-free water.

Prepare the 8% first dimension gel using the UreaGel system for 10 mL, mixing 3.2 mL of UreaGel concentrate, 5.8 mL of UreaGel diluent, 1 mL of UreaGel buffer, and adding 4 μL TEMED and 80 μL 10% APS just before pouring.
Use a comb with 15 wells for each lane in the first dimension gel.
To each 10 μL sample add 10 μL GBLII loading dye.
Load 200 ng dsRNA ladder as molecular weight marker into the first dimension gel.
Run the first dimension gel at 30 W for 7~8 mins in 0.5X TBE.
Stain the gel with 2 μL of SYBR Gold in 20 mL 0.5X TBE after electrophoresis.
Incubate the stained gel for 5 min.
Image the gel using 300 nm transillumination.
Excise each lane between 50 nt to topside from the first dimension gel.

Prepare the 16% second dimension gel using the UreaGel system for 20 mL, mixing 12.8 mL of UreaGel concentrate, 5.2 mL of UreaGel diluent, 2 mL of UreaGel buffer, and adding 8 μL TEMED and 160 μL 10% APS just before pouring.
Put the square plate horizontally and arrange gel slices in a “head-to-toe” manner with 2–5 mm gap between them.
Leave 1 cm space at the top of the notched plate for the second dimension gel to encapsulate the first dimension gel slices.
Apply 20–50 μL 0.5X TBE buffer on each gel slice to avoid air bubbles when placing the notched plate on top of the gel slices.
Remove excess TBE buffer after assembling the cassette, leaving 2 mm space at the bottom of the notched plate for pouring the second dimension gel.
Pour and gel solution from the bottom of the plates while slightly tilting the plates to one side to avoid air bubbles.
Use ~60°C prewarmed 0.5X TBE buffer to fill the electrophoresis chamber to facilitate denaturation of the cross-linked RNA.
Run the second dimension at 30 W for 50 min, starting around 300 V and gradually increasing to 500 V while the current starts around 100 mA and decreases to 60 mA.
Stain the gel with SYBR Gold after electrophoresis.
Excise the gel containing the cross-linked RNA from the 2D gel.
Transfer the excised gel to a new 10 cm cell culture dish.
Crush the gel by grinding with the cap of a 15 mL tube.
Add 300 μL crushing buffer to the gel debris.
Transfer the gel slurry to a 15 mL tube using a cell scraper.
Add additional 1.2 mL crushing buffer and rotate at room temperature overnight.
Transfer approximately 0.5 mL gel slurry to a Spin-X 0.45 μm column.
Spin the column at room temperature, 3400X g for 1 min until all gel slurry is filtered.
Aliquot 500 μL of the filtered RNA sample to an Amicon 10 k 0.5 mL column.
Spin the column at 12,000 X g for 5 min and repeat until all filtered RNA sample has passed through.
Wash the column with 300 μL water and spin the column at 12,000X g for 5 min.
Invert and place the column in a new collection tube.
Spin the column at 6000 X g for 5 min to recover approximately 85 μL RNA from each column (totaling approximately 170 μL from two columns).
Precipitate the RNA using the standard ethanol precipitation method with glycogen as a carrier.
Alternatively, purify the RNA using Zymo RNA clean and concentrator-5 columns.
Reconstitute the RNA in 11 μL water.
Dilute 1 μL of the RNA sample for Bioanalyzer analysis.
Add 10 μL of proximity ligation mixture to 10 μL of RNA.
Mix well and incubate at 65°C for 20 minutes.
Incubate the sample at 85°C for 5 minutes to inactivate the enzyme.
Add Proteinase K to 1 mg/mL, and incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Add 2 μL of 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.3), 2 μL of GlycoBlue, 25 μL of phenol, and 60 μL of isopropanol to the mixture.
Mix well and spin at 12,000 x g for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Wash the pellet twice with 70% ethanol.
Resuspend the RNA in 8 μL of RNase-free water.
Add 2 μL of 25 mM acridine orange to reverse AMT cross-linking.
Irradiate the sample with 254 nm UV for 30 minutes.
Heat reverse crosslinked RNA at 80°C for 90s, then snap cooling on ice.
Add 14 μL of adapter ligation mixture to 6 μL RNA and perform the adapter ligation reaction for 3 h at room temperature.

Mix 2.0 μL of 10x T4 RNA ligase buffer with 2.0 μL of 0.1 M DTT, 5.0 μL of 50 v/v % PEG8000, 2.0 μL of DMSO, 3.0 μL of 10 μM ddc RNA adapter, and 1.0 μL of High Concentration T4 RNA ligase to prepare the ligation mixture.
Add 3 μL of 10X RecJf buffer, 2 μL of RecJf, 1 μL of 5’ deadenylase, 1 μL of SuperaseIn, and 3 μL water to each sample after adapter ligation. Incubate at 37°C for 1 h.
Add 20 μL of water to each sample (total volume of 50 μL) and purify RNA with Zymo RNA clean and Concentrator-5 or ethanol precipitation.
Reconstitute RNA in 11 μL of RNase-free water (elute in 6 μL of water, use same 6 μL twice).
Heat the samples to 65°C for 5 min.
Chill the samples rapidly on ice.
Add 7.5 µL of reverse transcriptase mix to the RNA.
Incubate at 25°C for 15 min.
Incubate at 42°C for 10 hours.
Incubate at 80°C for 10 min.
Hold at 10°C.
Add 1 μL RNase H and RNase A/T1 mix.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 min at 1000 rpm in a thermomixer.
Purify the cDNA using SPRI DNA beads.
Add 2x volume of SPRI DNA beads to the sample.
Add equal volume of isopropanol, mix well.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
Let the beads settle on the magnet for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and wash the beads once with 80% ethanol (200 µL) at room temperature.
Dry the beads for 2 min.
Elute twice with 8.5 μL water to recover approximately 16 μL of cDNA.
Alternatively, using DNA Zymo concentrator-5 columns:
Add 7x Binding Buffer to the sample.
Add equal volume (8x original) of 100% EtOH to bind.
Wash normal.
Elute in 2 x 8.5 µL of water.
Add 4 μL circularization reaction mix to the cDNA sample.
Incubate at 60°C for 100 min, followed by 80°C for 10 min.
Add 21.4 μL of PCR Tall mix and run PCR program until exponential amplification is confirmed.
Transfer cDNA to optical PCR tubes when the fluorescence signal reaches a defined point.
Set up qPCR program with SYBR, initial 98°C for 2 mins, followed by 10 cycles of: 98°C for 15 s; 65°C for 30 s; 72°C for 45s, detect fluorescence at extension step.
Take sample out once amplification reaches exponential phase.
Transfer PCR product to a 1.5 mL tube.
Purify the DNA using SPRI DNA beads by adding 2x volume of SPRI DNA beads and mixing well.
Let the beads settle on the magnet for 5 min, then remove the supernatant.
Wash the beads once with 80% ethanol (200 μL) at RT.
Dry the sample for 2 min.
Elute twice with 10.5 μL water to recover ~20 μL.
Repeat SPRI DNA beads purification one more time.
Pool elute and add 21 μL of 2X PCR Solexa mix.
Run PCR reaction at 98°C for 2 minutes, followed by 3 cycles of 98°C for 15 seconds, 70°C for 30 seconds, and 72°C for 45 seconds. Hold at 4°C after the last cycle.
Purify reaction using standard Zymo concentrator-5 column protocol. Elute with 2x 8.5 μL of water and add 3 μL of Orange G loading dye.
Run a 6% native TBE gel at 200 V for 30 minutes, until the dye just runs off the gel. Load 50 bp ladder (NEB).
Stain gel in SYBR Gold for 3 minutes. Image gel at exposure times of 0.5, 1, and 2 seconds.
Cut out the DNA from 175 bp and above (corresponding to > 40 bp insert).
Use a syringe needle to punch a hole in the bottom of a 0.65 mL tube.
Transfer the gel slice to 0.65 mL tube and insert into a 2 mL collection tube. Spin at room temperature, 16,000X g for 5 minutes. The gel slice gets sheared into slurry by passing through the hole.
Remove the 0.65 mL tube and add 300 μL of Gel elute buffer to the slurry. Shake at 55°C, 1000 rpm overnight in a thermomixer.
Pass the gel slurry through a Spin-X 0.45 μm column to recover the DNA library.
Add 5x volume of Zymo DNA binding buffer to the sample.
Flow through Zymo concentrator-5 column.
Wash with 200 μL washing buffer once.
Elute twice with 8 μL water to recover approximately 15 μL library.
Quantify the library using a high sensitivity Bioanalyzer assay.
Pool barcoded libraries together for sequencing if necessary.
Sequence the libraries on an Illumina sequencer using standard conditions and P6_Custom_seqPrimer.
Perform a 70 nt single-end sequencing reaction, typically sufficient for PARIS.
Sequence multiplexing and random barcodes along with the insert.
